name: SR 28 over Little Wea Creek

type.deck: cast-in-place concrete slab, monolithic wearing surface, epoxy-coated reinforcing

substructure.type: concrete abutment on steel-encased concrete piles, riprap slope
pile bent: 9 steel-encased concrete piles (black epoxy coating), cap integral with slab
pile bent: 9 steel-encased concrete piles (black epoxy coating), cap integral with slab
concrete abutment on piles, riprap slope

joints.type: poured silicone, transverse at both bents

railing.type: reinforced concrete parapet on thick slab coping

geometry_ft.approach_guardrail: W-beam steel guardrail with posts, both approaches, transitions to the parapets

model_notes: Short 3-span flat slab on pile bents, 20 deg skew; the slab edge shows as a deep coping with the parapet on top (photos 1, 2, 17).
Piles are round, black-coated, about 14 in. diameter, ~9 per bent at ~4.5 ft spacing, standing in shallow water (photos 22, 25-28).
Banks are riprap under the bridge, grass beyond; flat farmland with bare winter fields and a tree line (photos 3-4, 14, 34).
Deck drains: 4 in. PVC spouts through the slab near the copings (photos 18, 23, 31).
